script: Good morning, this is Stocksplain for Thursday, November 26. We begin with a strong economic update as third quarter gross domestic product growth was revised upward to four and three-tenths percent, marking the strongest pace in three years. At the same time, inflation remains a prominent story. The Personal Consumption Expenditures price index rose three and eight-tenths percent over the past year, matching consumer spending and keeping pressure on household budgets as families navigate higher energy and holiday costs. In the tech sector, Nvidia shares dropped five percent following the return of chief executive Jensen Huang. Markets are working through a broad repositioning away from overcrowded technology trades, and credit agencies have issued warnings regarding corporate governance and debt levels. Analysts note that while underlying demand for chips remains extremely high, companies funding expensive artificial intelligence infrastructure through borrowed money face rising risks. Finally, the construction industry continues to face long-term challenges, with worker productivity falling forty percent since nineteen seventy due to local regulations and fragmentation. Today, we are looking at financial leverage. Financial leverage simply means using borrowed money to fund business operations or investments. While it can magnify your gains when times are good, it also increases your risk. If a company takes on too much debt to build expensive projects and revenue slows down, those interest payments do not go away. That is why heavy leverage makes companies much more sensitive to credit rating warnings and market pullbacks. Thank you for listening, and have a wonderful day.
